findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupAdapter.java:274 — getSubGroupsCount() returns null when model is gone, risking NPE on auto-unboxing/arithmetic; return 0 or throw ModelIllegalStateException instead
[Medium/concurrency] GroupTest.java:createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti — reader thread is never joined and may still be executing against the realm after test returns, causing flaky failures
[Medium/performance] GroupTest.java — reader thread busy-spins with no sleep/backoff, hammering the admin endpoint thousands of times; add sleep or bounded iterations
[Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java — test may exit before reader thread performs a single read, allowing the assertion to pass vacuously with no synchronization guaranteeing at least one read

[Low/concurrency] GroupTest.java — caughtExceptions collects any exception type (e.g., 404 on deleted group, auth hiccups), making the assertion overly broad and potentially masking the actual NPE bug; assert on specific NPE or empty-result invariant
[Low/bug] GroupTest.java — deletedAll.set(true) is outside try/finally, so if a delete throws, the non-daemon reader thread loops forever, leaking a thread and hanging JVM shutdown
[Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java — no unit-level test covers the null-count return path in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(); the changed behavior is only indirectly exercised

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] GroupTest.java — reader thread busy-spins with no sleep/backoff, hammering the admin endpoint thousands of times; add sleep or bounded iterations

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, a reader thread is started that loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` and repeatedly calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` with no sleep/backoff or bounded iterations. This is a verifiable busy-spin that can hammer the admin endpoint and cause unnecessary load, slow/flaky tests, or timeouts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java — test may exit before reader thread performs a single read, allowing the assertion to pass vacuously with no synchronization guaranteeing at least one read

adjudication.rationale: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread is started but never synchronized with the main thread (no `join()`, latch, or other barrier), and the loop condition `while (!deletedAll.get())` can become false before the thread performs any `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call. Since `caughtExceptions` only records exceptions from that loop, the final `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` can pass even if no reads occurred, making the test potentially vacuous.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] GroupTest.java — caughtExceptions collects any exception type (e.g., 404 on deleted group, auth hiccups), making the assertion overly broad and potentially masking the actual NPE bug; assert on specific NPE or empty-result invariant

adjudication.rationale: In the added test, the background thread catches any Exception and adds it to caughtExceptions, and the test asserts the list is empty (i.e., it fails on any exception). This does not “mask” an NPE; an NPE would be captured and cause the final assertion to fail. The mention of specific expected exception types like 404/auth hiccups is speculative and not grounded in the diff (the thread only calls groups().groups(...) list API, not per-group fetches).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] GroupTest.java — deletedAll.set(true) is outside try/finally, so if a delete throws, the non-daemon reader thread loops forever, leaking a thread and hanging JVM shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In GroupTest.createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), a non-daemon reader thread is started (`new Thread(...).start()`) and it stops only when `deletedAll` becomes true. `deletedAll.set(true)` is executed only after the deletion loop, with no try/finally. If any `managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, the test will abort before setting the flag, leaving the reader thread looping indefinitely and potentially hanging the JVM/test run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java — no unit-level test covers the null-count return path in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(); the changed behavior is only indirectly exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` to potentially return `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` is `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). The only added test (`GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`) is a concurrent create/read/delete integration test that asserts no exceptions, but it does not directly assert or cover the specific new null-return branch of `getSubGroupsCount()` (e.g., behavior when the underlying model is missing). This is a specific test gap tied to the new conditional logic.
